newsitem.title: FRANCE: Mobutu's plane standing by at French airport.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu's plane standing by at French airport.

text.p: The personal plane of ailing Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has arrived in Nice, southern France, and is standing by to take him home to his war-racked country, airport officials said on Wednesday.

France expressed worry on Wednesday over events in Zaire, where rebels are advancing rapidly in the east aiming to topple the 66-year-old president, and said it was taking measures to protect its citizens.
"The current uncertainties have led us to take the necessary measures concerning the security of our citizens," said foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt at a regular briefing.
"We are in close communication with our European and American partners," he added. He gave no further details.
Nice airport officials said Mobutu's white Boeing 727 and a cargo plane for his belongings arrived at the Riviera airport on Tuesday night.

Mobutu, in power for almost 32 years, was admitted to a hospital in nearby Monaco at the weekend. He has spent most of his time in Europe since undergoing prostate cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.
The officials said no date was set for the president's return, which has repeatedly been announced as imminent by his entourage, only to be delayed for medical reasons.

However the plane's arrival lent credence to his son and spokesman Mobutu Nzanga's statements that the veteran strongman was determined to return to Zaire and make a stand against the ethnic Tutsi-dominated rebels led by Laurent Kabila, who have captured more than one-fifth of the sprawling country.
Mobutu Nzanga said on Tuesday that the president was able to walk and feed himself and would soon leave hospital.
He has repeatedly denied reports that his father is in a serious or critical condition, saying such reports were part of a political manipulation to remove him from office.
Rummelhardt said the attempt on Tuesday by Zaire's parliamentary opposition to oust Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo, was a particular concern.
Kengo is in Kenya where African leaders opened a meeting in Nairobi on Wednesday on the Zaire crisis with a strong call for negotiations to end the war tearing apart the country.
The Congolese Red Cross said on Tuesday that members of Mobutu's family had taken refuge across the Zaire river in neighbouring Congo in the face of advances by the rebels.
